speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child with a low-grade fever, an itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics. Can you tell me the specific name of the antibiotic you took and when you started feeling these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-induced serum sickness-like reaction.

I have noted the details from your history: an 8-year-old girl with a one-week history of amoxicillin use for sinusitis, followed by a low-grade fever, itchy rash spreading from joints to the trunk, and generalized joint pain starting just two days ago. Given the timing relative to the antibiotic and the specific pattern of symptoms, do you recall any other medications or exposures she might have had in the past few weeks?
